title: Orecchiette con salsiccia
subtitle: Pugliese ear pasta with Italian sausage and broccoli
excerpt: Orecchiette con salsiccia is a Pugliese staple: the small ear-shaped pasta tossed with crumbled pork sausage, broccoli, garlic, and chilli. The sausage and broccoli are cooked in the same pan, and the pasta water binds everything into a loose, savoury sauce. It is a very forgiving dish to make and one that improves if you use good sausages.
sourceNotes: Pugliese regional recipe. Orecchiette with broccoli and sausage is one of the most popular pasta dishes in Puglia. Method drawn from traditional Pugliese cooking sources and Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (2001).

glossaryTerms.definition: Small, dome-shaped pasta from Puglia whose name means 'little ears'; the concave shape cups sauces and small pieces of meat or vegetable.

content.text: Orecchiette con salsiccia is a Pugliese weeknight dish: small ear-shaped

tossed with crumbled pork sausage, broccoli florets, garlic, and chilli. The pasta and the broccoli cook together, then both go into the pan with the sausage. The starchy pasta water and the sausage fat make a sauce without any cream. It comes together in under 30 minutes.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Crumble in {{sausage-meat}} of sausagemeat and cook, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and {{chilli-flakes}} of chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute more.
Cook the pasta and broccoli, then finish

Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli florets and cook for 2 minutes. Add {{pasta-dried}} of orecchiette and cook until al dente, following the packet time. Reserve a large mug of pasta water, then drain.

Tip the pasta and broccoli into the frying pan with the sausage. Toss over medium heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time, until everything is coated in a light, glossy sauce. Season with salt. Serve with Parmesan if you like, though in Puglia it is often eaten without.

items.fix: Add broccoli for only 2 minutes; it will soften further in the frying pan. Some pieces collapsing into the sauce is traditional.
Add pasta water generously. The starch it carries is what makes the sauce.

items.cause: Fat not properly rendered or pan too cold.
items.fix: Start with a hot pan. Pour off excess fat after browning if needed, leaving 2 tablespoons.

content.text: Orecchiette are the pasta of Puglia, shaped by pressing the thumb across small pieces of semolina dough. The combination with broccoli rabe (cime di rapa) is the classic; with pork sausage is the popular alternative that most home cooks make on a weeknight. It is a dish that needs no special technique and scales easily to feed a crowd.
